reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: The intervention successfully engaged its target - malignant lymphoid cells were targeted through sequential high-dose chemotherapy and allogeneic immune effect. Evidence includes successful donor engraftment with median 95% donor chimerism at day 100, demonstrating the allogeneic component was established. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The intended biological pathway was activated - the tandem approach provided both cytoreductive effect (autologous transplant) and immune-mediated anti-tumor effect (allogeneic transplant). Neutrophil recovery at 12 days indicates successful hematopoietic reconstitution. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The primary endpoint of ≥80% donor chimerism at day 100 was met with 95% chimerism achieved. More importantly, clinical outcomes showed superior results for patients completing both transplants (2-year PFS 72%, OS 89%) compared to autologous only (2-year PFS 46%, OS 69%). 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Clear benefit was seen in the subgroup completing both transplants versus those receiving only autologous transplant, validating the tandem approach mechanism. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Manageable safety profile with acceptable rates of GVHD and non-relapse mortality for this high-risk population.

failure_modes.evidence: While the primary endpoint was met overall, the clinical benefit was primarily seen in patients who completed both transplants versus those who received only autologous transplant
